problems.problem: The bottom plaque band still renders in plain Arial (spec title.font C:/Windows/Fonts/arial.ttf; the georgia group was REJECTED last round), and the visible glyphs confirm it: 'TOBACCO VANILLE' at 86px sits with default tracking and loose line stacking (logo bbox [454,1073,603,1093], title [151,1152,946,1216], subtitle [324,1296,569,1318]). Against the Chanel N°5 reference plaque, whose authority comes from tight, wide-tracked capitals in a disciplined band, this reads as a generic default stack; the concept's sans family is fine, but the execution needs a tracked grotesque plaque, not untouched Arial metrics.

The decoration rule (y=1040, 3px below product base 1037) still collides with the contact zone. In the contact detail crop [266,897,815,1147] the crisp dark rule runs through the soft shadow smudge under the glass, so the bottle appears to stand on a drawn line rather than on paper; the brief wants the fine silver line as a separator above the brand word with clear daylight between base, shadow and rule. Decoration is not a patchable field, so the fix must come from moving the product block up to open a gap.

The regenerated silver-gelatin wash now shows a smoother charcoal-to-mineral drift than the previous flat grey (visible top-to-bottom tonal slope in image 1 vs image 7), but at poster scale the promised fine photographic grain and edge vignette are still imperceptible and the mid-field stays a cool neutral; against the Chanel plate's rich paper gradient the field still reads slightly digital. Deepening the top charcoal and warming the mineral bottom would also seat the dark ink band better.

Contact shadow is present and correctly seated (offset_y 0; detail crop shows the smudge directly under the base, no floating), and opacity 0.45/blur 12 improved the anchor versus the previous timid 0.35. However under a near-black glass base on mid-grey paper the smudge still dissipates too fast laterally: the base corners in the crop lose their anchor tone within a few pixels, so the bottle's weight reads lighter than the reference plates.

changes.value: Seamless matte silver-gelatin photographic paper wash, smooth vertical gradient from deep charcoal grey at top through mid silver to pale warm mineral grey at bottom, pronounced chemical tonal drift, clearly visible fine photographic grain, soft edge vignette, broad diffuse frontal illumination with gentle top-down falloff, completely empty, no objects, no horizon line
